newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Arabs seek U.N. meeting on Israel housing plan.
newsitem.headline: Arabs seek U.N. meeting on Israel housing plan.

text.p: The Arab group has asked for an urgent Security Council meeting to halt an Israeli plan to build 132 housing units for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem.

The request, circulated on Wednesday by the group's chairman, Iraqi ambassador Nizar Hamdoon, followed a letter to the council last Friday from the Palestine Liberation Organisation's U.N. observer, Nasser al-Kidwa, also calling for council action but not requesting a formal meeting.

Hamdoon said implementation of the Israeli plan for the Ras al-Amud district of East Jerusalem and the continuation of Israel's settlement policy "threaten to have serious consequences for peace and security in the region."
He called on the council to "convene an urgent meeting in order to take the measures that are needed in order to put an end to the Israeli government's pln with respect to building settlements."
Israel captured East Jerusalem from Jordan during the 1967 Middle East war and later declared the undivided city its capital.
Security Council President Francesco Paolo Fulci of Italy called in Israeli charge d'affaires David Peleg Tuesday to express the council's concern.
Fulci told reporters Wednesday that council members were considering the issue on the basis of preliminary information provided by the Israeli envoy.
Asked whether the council would hold a formal meeting, he said: "That is being seriously considered."

Fulci said he told Peleg that "for the first time on this matter we showed unanimity, real unanimity, in the council. No dissenting voice," he said, implying the United States also opposed the Israeli plan to build in East Jerusalem.
"That is something that I think should be taken into serious consideration," he said, adding that further information was awaited from the Israeli envoy.
